A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SupGCL study. The main texts, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive reformatting and appendix expansion.

before.justification: v4 reports original downstream-task experiments, embedding analyses, link prediction, robustness tests and biological enrichment analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experiments and adds results for additional comparators, sampling sizes, pan-cancer pretraining and perturbation variants.

M1.justification: The central objective, shared encoder and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix F.4 additionally defines an optional node-sampled approximation, including sampled graph similarities and the resulting loss in Eqs. (20)–(23), extending the augmentation sampling already described in v4. This does not establish a change to the default experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions use TCGA/LINCS GRNs for breast, lung and colorectal cancer and retain the same gene-annotation, survival, subtype and link-prediction tasks. The added pan-cancer experiment pools already covered cancers; the additional sampling and perturbation experiments vary settings within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v5 Table 30 retains GCA, AFGRL and SimGRACE from v4 Table 16 and adds AD-GCL, AutoGCL, ArieL, Geneformer under three fine-tuning regimes, and adapted MuSe-GNN. Appendix H also adds GRACE to the corresponding cross-domain fine-tuning and OOD comparisons.

E3.justification: The original benchmark protocols remain, but substantial additional evaluation settings are introduced: pooled three-cancer pretraining with breast-only downstream evaluation, augmentation-normalizer sample sizes of 8/16/32/40, asymmetric patient/teacher edge thresholds, alternative perturbation operations, and three Geneformer freezing regimes. These are added protocols, not evidence that the retained benchmarks were rerun under changed settings.

E4.justification: New analyses test sensitivity to augmentation sampling size, node-copy versus directional edge perturbations, asymmetric teacher/patient GRN noise, and pooled-cancer pretraining. Adding matched GRACE cross-domain results also tests whether transfer failures are specific to SupGCL. Earlier temperature, embedding-dimension, data-size and enrichment analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 3 changes from point-valued NMI/ARI results to values with ± variability across five pretraining runs. v4 does not state a corresponding run count, so this establishes newly reported replication and uncertainty, not an explicit increase from a known count. Existing cross-validation, seed reporting and Bonferroni-corrected tests remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The 13 primary task scores and most matched appendix results are unchanged. Numerous results are added for the new comparisons and analyses. Figure 3 replaces SupGCL's NMI/ARI values of 0.117/0.150 with five-run summaries of 0.155±0.013/0.121±0.007; these are differently aggregated results, not demonstrated same-run performance changes.

T1.justification: The original KL-decomposition theorem and limiting corollary are retained. New Appendix F adds computational-complexity derivations, sampling-bias Propositions F.1–F.2 and Lemmas F.3–F.4, with small-inverse-temperature and node-independence assumptions. Appendix L.1 adds a teacher-copying counterexample to unconstrained learned augmentation.

C1.justification: The biological-supervision contribution and superiority claim across 13 downstream tasks remain. v5 narrows the theoretical special-case claim explicitly to node-level GCL and elevates embedding-space clustering into the abstract, contribution list and conclusion. These refine the central contribution rather than replace it.

C2.justification: v5 adds substantive discussion of LINCS off-target noise and aggregation tradeoffs, Geneformer's domain mismatch, learned-augmentation degeneracy and perturbation fidelity. Cross-domain failure is interpreted using GRACE as a broader GCL limitation, with pooled pretraining presented as preliminary mitigation. The Impact Statement also explicitly limits causal and clinical interpretations.

D1.justification: v5 newly discloses the default augmentation sampling size of eight and independent sampling sizes for normalization and loss calculation. It also documents Geneformer's 316M model, 18 layers, 1152-dimensional embeddings and freezing regimes, plus the separate encoders and reconstruction/InfoNCE losses of adapted MuSe-GNN. Original hardware, hyperparameters and runtime records are retained.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to augmentation-adjustment methods and statistical formulations of supervised contrastive learning. New positioning against AD-GCL, AutoGCL, ArieL, SupCon, Geneformer and virtual gene-perturbation approaches broadens the novelty argument beyond the earlier emphasis on augmentation-free GCL and GRN representation learning.

P1.justification: v5 substantially reframes the narrative around embedding analysis followed by fine-tuning, rewriting the abstract, contributions and conclusion and reordering the experimental subsections. Appendices are reorganized into dedicated computational-analysis and comparison sections, and an Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout. The node- and graph-task tables are merged, the task-description table moves to the appendix, Figure 3 gains repeated-run annotations, and several new tables are introduced. Most underlying plots are retained despite relocation and resizing.

improvement.justification: Additional comparators, especially MuSe-GNN using both patient and teacher graphs, repeated-run clustering statistics and targeted ablations strengthen validation and reproducibility. The gains are tempered by breast-only pan-cancer evaluation and problems in the new material: Tables 6 and 26 disagree on the breast LINCS edge count, and Proposition F.2 predicts vanishing sampling bias although the defined losses retain a log(|V|/|V_B|) difference under uniform predictions. The retained core study gains useful support, but the additions do not establish a substantial overall improvement.
